question: Why are perfect numbers also triangles and stacks of odd cubes?
answer: Each perfect number 2^(p−1)(2^p−1) lands on a triangle with 2^p−1 rows, so it holds exactly that many dots: the perfect-number formula itself. The first m odd cubes add to m²(2m²−1), which is the same formula when m² = 2^(p−1). So one shape can be seen as a triangle or as a stack of odd cubes.
move: 2 p−1 (2 p −1) is one shape seen two ways: a triangle and a stack of odd cubes.
